mutations.from: authService.createAuthSessionPayload(tx, user, context, { orgId: row.orgId, ssoOrgId: row.orgId, expectedEpoch: row.user.credentialEpoch ?? 0 }),
mutations.to: authService.createAuthSessionPayload(tx, user, context, { orgId: row.orgId, ssoOrgId: row.orgId }),
mutations.expect: R2 finding 1/3 (race): the complete queued behind the epoch bump answers 200 with tokens at the new epoch (the user row it re-read after the bump committed) and a refresh session is written, instead of 401 SESSION_REVOKED

mutations.name: R2-F11 the first SSO binding is written by id alone again (the ssoSubject: null condition dropped)
mutations.expect: R2 finding 11 (race): both queued callbacks link (count 1 each) and both issue tickets; the later write overwrites the first binding, so there is no SSO_IDENTITY_CONFLICT loser and W's ticket count rises by 2

mutations.name: R3-F3a the callback writes its ticket without the epoch hold (holdCredentialEpoch removed from the ticket transaction)
mutations.to: // (mutant) the callback's ticket is written without holding the identity at the epoch it read
mutations.expect: R3 item 3 (race): the callback never waits (no waiter behind the held User row; waitForBlocked gives up after 20 s with 0, no FOR NO KEY UPDATE waiter) and redirects to /sso/complete with a ticket instead of /sign-in?ssoError=SESSION_REVOKED; V's SsoTicket count rises by 1 while the bump is still held. R3 item 3 (control) still passes.

mutations.name: R3-F3b the callback's ticket is written outside the epoch-hold transaction, before the hold (prisma.ssoTicket.create on its own connection, then the hold)
mutations.to: await prisma.ssoTicket.create({ data: { orgId: org.id, userId: user.id, tokenHash: hashToken(ticket), expiresAt: new Date(Date.now() + TICKET_TTL_MS), ipAddress: context.ipAddress || null, ...(membership ? { membershipId: membership.id } : {}) } }); await require("./auth.service").holdCredentialEpoch(tx, user.id, Number.isInteger(user.credentialEpoch) ? user.credentialEpoch : 0); return;
mutations.expect: R3 item 3 (race): the callback still waits at the hold and still redirects with ssoError=SESSION_REVOKED, but the ticket row was already committed outside the transaction: V's SsoTicket count is before+1 while the bump is held and after it commits (the 'no SsoTicket row written' part fails). R3 item 3 (control) still passes (one ticket, it redeems).

mutations.name: R3-F3c the callback checks the epoch with a plain read inside the ticket transaction instead of the row lock
mutations.to: { const seen = await tx.user.findUnique({ where: { id: user.id }, select: { credentialEpoch: true, status: true } }); if (!seen || seen.status !== "active" || seen.credentialEpoch !== (Number.isInteger(user.credentialEpoch) ? user.credentialEpoch : 0)) throw new HttpError(401, "SESSION_REVOKED", "This session has ended; sign in again"); }
mutations.expect: R3 item 3 (race): the read sees the last committed epoch (the bump is uncommitted), so the callback never waits (0 waiters after 20 s), writes the ticket and redirects to /sso/complete instead of ssoError=SESSION_REVOKED; V's SsoTicket count rises by 1. R3 item 3 (control) still passes.

mutations.name: R3-F3d the epoch hold no longer locks the User row (FOR NO KEY UPDATE dropped from holdCredentialEpoch)
mutations.from: const rows = await tx.$queryRaw`SELECT "id" FROM "User" WHERE "id" = ${userId} AND "credentialEpoch" = ${epoch} AND "status" = 'active' FOR NO KEY UPDATE`;
mutations.to: const rows = await tx.$queryRaw`SELECT "id" FROM "User" WHERE "id" = ${userId} AND "credentialEpoch" = ${epoch} AND "status" = 'active'`;
mutations.expect: R3 item 3 (race): the hold reads the pre-bump row without waiting (0 waiters after 20 s), the ticket is written and the callback redirects to /sso/complete instead of ssoError=SESSION_REVOKED; V's SsoTicket count rises by 1. R3 item 3 (control) still passes. (R2 finding 1/3 (race) is not expected to fail here: complete() queues on its lastLogin update of T's row, and the unlocked hold then reads the committed bump and refuses.)

mutations.name: R3-CTL the callback holds a stale epoch (one below the epoch it read), so every SSO callback is refused
mutations.expect: R3 item 3 (control): the non-racing callback redirects to /sign-in?ssoError=SESSION_REVOKED with no ticket (no SsoTicket row, redeem of the placeholder 401 SSO_TICKET_INVALID, no /auth/me). Collateral: R3 item 3 (race) fails too (the hold's WHERE filters the row out before locking, so it is refused at once and no waiter is seen), and every check that needs an SSO ticket (C10 Q and G, C13 P via Y and via X, C14 with the Y-SSO bearer, R2 fresh sign-ins, tickets and the binding race) fails with SESSION_REVOKED at the callback.

mutations.name: R4-LEGACY the callback's legacy branch materialises the Y row without the (org, e-mail) advisory lock
mutations.to: // (mutant) the legacy branch writes the membership row without the (org, e-mail) lock
mutations.expect: R4 legacy SSO vs deactivation (race): the callback never queues at the held (Y, e-mail) lock (callback queued 0, no advisory waiter; the wait ends as soon as it answers) and, while the proof still holds the lock, G2's Y row is written active and a ticket is issued (Y row present while held, G2 tickets before+1 while held). The deactivation then queues alone (both queued 1, one advisory waiter), suspends the row and voids the ticket, so the outcome parts (200, suspended, redeem 401 SSO_TICKET_INVALID, no Y session) still hold; the serialisation parts fail. C10 legacy (G) still passes (no contention).
